name: Great Western Schism
summary: Disputed election produces two rival popes, Urban VI in Rome and Clement VII in Avignon, each backed by competing royal courts. A third claimant emerges from the Council of Pisa in 1409. The Council of Constance ends the schism in 1417 with the election of Martin V.

_quarry.structural_significance: Permanently undermines the late-medieval doctrine of papal mon-archy; the conciliarist movement gains ground; Bohemian (Hussite) and English (Lollard) reformers exploit the discredit.
